section: Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India 1968
title: ## ALL-INDIA SURVEY During 1968, 1,26,232 deaths were reported in India which had resulted from accidents of various types. The causes of accidents have been classified into two broad categories viz. (i) Accidents due to acts of nature such as snake bite, animal killing, floods, land-slides etc. and (ii) Accidents due to other causes such as mishaps in factories, air crashes, railway accidents etc. The detailed break-up of such accidental deaths in the country due to various causes is furnished in Table I. This Table shows that deaths due to acts of nature accounted for 26·9% of the total accidental deaths. Railway accidents and accidents on the roads accounted for 6·3% and 4·8% of the total accidental deaths respectively. Quite a substantial number of persons (4,581)died because of animal bite/killing. The most prominent accidental killer was drowning accounting for 23·1% of all such deaths. The pattern of the percentage distribution of accidental deaths due to various causes is more or less the same as during 1966 and 1967, except that deaths due to poisoning registered a sharp rise of about 37% over 1967. This constituted 6·3% of the total accidental deaths during 1968 as against 4·7% and 4·2% during 1966 and 1967 respectively. TABLE I
